evals.prompt: ok can you do a full editorial pass on the rust-ruined-javascript-result post — i don't want any edits applied, just generate the report so i can read it first
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers from the natural-language request, resolves the slug to content/blog/posts/rust-ruined-javascript-result.mdx, dispatches all four subagents in parallel using scratch mode (no edits applied), aggregates the four partial reports into .scratch/editorialize-rust-ruined-javascript-result.md with the four sections in the documented order, and prints a final summary showing 0 applied / N deferred / report path. The post itself must remain unmodified.

assertions.text: aggregated report file is written under .scratch/
report contains all four section headers in documented order
final summary uses scratch mode and reports zero applied

evals.prompt: i wrote a quick draft at .scratch/seeded-factual-errors.mdx (frontmatter title='seeded errors', description='test', authorGithubUsername='zrosenbauer', readTime=1, publishedAt='2026-05-13'). the body says 'JavaScript is a classical language. Rust was created at Mozilla in 2005 by Graydon Hoare.' please create that file then run the editorial pass on it in scratch mode so the post stays untouched and i just get the factcheck findings.
evals.expected_output: Agent creates the fixture, the skill resolves the relative path (.scratch/seeded-factual-errors.mdx), dispatches the factchecker subagent which uses Context7 + WebSearch to verify both claims and writes findings to .scratch/editorialize-seeded-factual-errors-factcheck.md. Both claims are flagged as wrong with corrections (JS is prototypal/multi-paradigm; Rust dates to 2006, first stable 2015) and at least one source URL per finding.

assertions.text: report uses the documented finding-line marker (✗) for wrong claims
factchecker correction explains JS is prototypal / multi-paradigm (not a verbatim restate of the prompt)
factchecker provides the correct Rust date (2006 project / 2015 stable)
each finding includes a source URL

report identifies pattern #1 (significance inflation) by number in heading
report identifies pattern #10 (rule of three) by number in heading
every finding includes a Before / After pair

evals.prompt: hey can u review my latest blog post real quick — i'm shipping it tomorrow and want a fact check before it goes out, just give me the report don't change the file
evals.expected_output: The skill should trigger from this casual phrasing (matches description triggers like 'edit my latest post' / 'review my most recent blog post' / 'fact check'). With no target arg, the skill prompts the user (via AskUserQuestion in Claude Code or numbered list elsewhere) to pick from the 4 most recent posts sorted by publishedAt. The 'just give me the report' phrasing should be interpreted as scratch mode. After the user picks (or the agent defaults to most recent), the four agents run and the .scratch/ report is written.

assertions.text: agent identifies the most recent post by publishedAt before dispatching
agent recognizes scratch mode from the 'don't change the file' phrasing
an aggregated report under .scratch/ exists with the editorialize- prefix
